gm_lines: A Waning Mark is not a condition. Immunity to a condition does not grant immunity to Waning Marks unless a feature says otherwise.

You can maintain a number of Waning Marks equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature can have only one Waning Mark from you at a time unless a feature says otherwise. A Waning Mark lasts until the end of your next turn, until you spend it, or until the marked creature is no longer on the same plane of existence as you.
Mark the Waning. As a Bonus Action, choose one creature within 60 feet that you can see, hear, or otherwise perceive clearly. The target gains one Waning Mark.

Receive Overextension. As a Reaction when a creature within 60 feet that you can perceive hits with an attack, forces a saving throw, regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, spends CP, uses a spell slot, teleports, or moves at least 10 feet during its turn, you may apply one Waning Mark to that creature after the triggering event resolves.
Withdrawing Thread damage: 1d6 at CL 1-4, 2d6 at CL 5-10, 3d6 at CL 11-16, 4d6 at CL 17-20.
Once per round, when a marked creature you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Waning Mark without using an Action. Choose one Diminishing Response appropriate to the trigger.
